title: Superannuation Calculator Salary: Convert Your Hourly Rate to Annual Pay with Casual Loading
description: Use our superannuation calculator salary tool to convert hourly rates to annual, fortnightly, and weekly pay. Includes casual loading, super guarantee, and tax estimates for 2026-2
salarySummary: Based on a 38-hour week, your annual gross pay is your hourly rate multiplied by 38 hours per week times 52 weeks, with superannuation paid on top at 12%.

faqs.q: How do I use the superannuation calculator salary tool?
faqs.a: Enter your base hourly rate on the timesheet (the home page). If you are a casual employee, check the 'Add 25% casual loading' box. The tool then calculates your annual gross, fortnightly pay, weekly pay, estimated superannuation (12% on top), and estimated tax using the 2026-27 resident tax scale and Medicare levy. It assumes a 38-hour week and no overtime or penalty rates.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the National Minimum Wage and award rates?
faqs.a: The National Minimum Wage is the legal minimum set by the Fair Work Commission, currently $26.44 per hour (from 1 July 2026) for a 38-hour week. Award rates are industry-specific minimums that often exceed the national minimum. Our superannuation calculator salary tool uses the hourly rate you enter, which may be an award rate or any other rate. It does not automatically apply award rates.

faqs.q: Does the superannuation calculator salary include tax?
faqs.a: Yes, it estimates tax using the 2026-27 resident tax brackets (nil up to $18,200, then 15%, 30%, 37%, 45%) plus the Medicare levy of 2%. However, it does not deduct HELP repayments, the Medicare levy surcharge, or salary packaging. The estimate also uses the 2025-26 single reduction thresholds for Medicare because the 2026-27 thresholds were not confirmed at the time of calculation. Always consult the Australian Taxation Office for your exact liability.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Your Hourly to Annual Conversion

If you are paid by the hour or considering a salary offer, our [superannuation calculator salary](/) tool helps you see the big picture. The basic formula is simple: multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then multiply by 52 weeks. For a standard full-time worker, we assume a 38-hour week, as set by the Fair Work Ombudsman. That gives you your annual gross pay before tax and super.

For example, if your hourly rate is $30.00 and you work 38 hours each week, your annual gross is $30.00 × 38 × 52 = $59,280. This is the figure you would see on a salary offer. But your total employment cost is higher because superannuation is paid on top.

### Using the Timesheet Calculator

On [the timesheet](/), you type your base hourly rate. If you are a casual employee, check the box to add 25% casual loading. The tool then applies the loading to your rate before calculating annual, fortnightly, and weekly figures. Never type a rate that already includes casual loading – the calculator handles that for you. Casual loading compensates for not receiving paid leave, and it is a common feature of award rates.

### Fortnightly Pay

Many Australian workers are paid fortnightly. To find your fortnightly gross, simply double your weekly pay. Using the same $30.00 rate, weekly pay is $30.00 × 38 = $1,140, so fortnightly is $2,280. The calculator shows both weekly and fortnightly amounts to help you budget.

## National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

The Fair Work Commission sets the National Minimum Wage. From 1 July 2026, it is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. For casuals, the minimum including 25% loading is $33.05 per hour. These are legal floors – most employees are covered by an award or registered agreement that sets higher rates. Our [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page explains the current rates. If you are unsure which rate applies, check your award on the Fair Work Ombudsman website or use our [pay guides](/blog) for guidance.

### Casual Loading and Super

Casual loading is paid on top of the base hourly rate. It is not superannuation. Superannuation (the super guarantee) is an additional 12% of your ordinary earnings, paid by your employer into a super fund. This is on top of your gross pay. For a $30.00 base rate, if you are casual with loading, your effective hourly rate becomes $37.50 ($30.00 + 25%). Your super is calculated on that loaded amount. The super guarantee applies up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per quarter (2026-27). Our [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page has more details.

## Tax and Take-Home Pay

Once you have your annual gross, the calculator estimates tax using the 2026-27 resident tax scale:
- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Plus the Medicare levy of 2% (with possible reductions for low-income earners). The calculator uses the 2025-26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026-27 thresholds were not confirmed. It does not deduct HELP loans, the Medicare levy surcharge, or salary packaging. For a more precise estimate, see our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) page.

### Example with Casual Loading

Suppose you are a casual earning a base rate of $28.00 per hour. With 25% loading, your casual rate is $35.00. For a 38-hour week, weekly gross is $1,330, fortnightly $2,660, and annual gross $69,160. Super at 12% on ordinary earnings adds $8,299.20 on top (subject to the maximum contribution base). Estimated tax (using the scale above) would be roughly $12,067 plus Medicare $1,383, leaving take-home around $55,710. These are estimates only.

## Average Earnings in Australia

The Australian Bureau of Statistics reports Average Weekly Earnings for full-time adult ordinary time at $2,083.70 per week (May 2026). That is an average across all industries and states, not a median for any specific job. Our [average pay](/topics/average-pay) page explains how to interpret these figures. If you are comparing your rate to an industry average, remember that averages can be skewed by high earners.

### When Your Hours Differ

The formula assumes you work the same number of hours every week. If you work fewer hours (e.g., 20 hours per week), adjust accordingly: annual gross = hourly rate × hours per week × 52. The calculator on [the timesheet](/) lets you change the hours assumption. For part-time or irregular hours, the annual figure is an estimate. Always check your actual pay slips.

## Important Disclaimer

Annual pay shown is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

For more detailed information, explore our [reference tables](/data) for tax brackets and super rates, or visit the [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) guide. If you need to compare your pay to industry standards, the [job pay](/topics/job-pay) page may help.
